Rugged tablet for BigChange JobWatch

BigChange describes itself as job management software built for UK field service teams, combining job handling, scheduling, vehicle tracking, customer service and billing in one system. The sectors on its site include plumbing, heating and HVAC, industrial doors, fire and security, facilities management, electrical contracting, equipment rental and hire, drainage, waste and environmental, and building maintenance. The office signs in to the BigChange system through a web login; engineers and drivers work from the JobWatch by BigChange mobile app.

The mobile app is where the work in the field is recorded. The vendor's field resource management page says the app works offline and can collect signatures without connectivity, that engineers capture and annotate photos, follow custom worksheets and workflows step by step, and that the worksheets handle data capture, photo capture and barcode scanning. It also says engineers can see the last 10 jobs done on a site and up to 90 previous photos. Much of that happens between the van and the customer's door, in the rain, in a cold yard or in a cab in full sun, which is where a consumer tablet tends to crack, fog or become unreadable.

This page sets out what BigChange publishes about the devices JobWatch runs on, what it does not publish, which Tuga rugged devices meet the published requirement, and how a UK field service business can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet.

Requirements

What BigChange needs from a device

Each item below comes from BigChange Limited's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 9 or later, from Google Play, on phones and tablets

    The Android app is published on Google Play as JobWatch by BigChange (package bigchangeapps.com.jobwatch, developer BigChange Limited). When checked on 15 October 2026 the listing showed version 5.38.0, updated 6 October 2026, with a minimum API level of 28 (Android 9), and device chips for Phone and Tablet. The vendor's field resource management page says the app is for both Android and iOS tablets and phones. Source: play.google.com

  • RAM, storage and screen size: not published

    No minimum or recommended RAM, storage or screen size for JobWatch was found on the vendor's site, its Google Play listing or the pages of its help guide that could be read. The vendor's help guide at support.bigchange.com loads its articles with JavaScript, so if your BigChange account manager or the help guide gives a device specification, check it against the figures below before you buy. Source: bigchange.com

  • Offline working, including signatures

    The vendor's field resource management page states that the field service app works offline and lets engineers collect signatures without connectivity. A vendor blog post from October 2023 adds that engineers can access job details even without a data connection. The vendor does not publish how much is cached on the device, how sync works when signal returns, or whether the device has to be online at the start of a shift. Source: bigchange.com

  • Worksheets, photos and barcode scanning in the app

    The same page describes custom worksheets and workflows that take engineers through a job step by step, with data capture, photo capture and barcode scanning, and says engineers can capture and annotate photos on site and view up to 90 previous photos and the last 10 jobs done at a site. The October 2023 blog post mentions scanning barcodes and QR codes. The vendor does not say whether scanning uses the camera or supports a dedicated scan engine, so plan on the camera. Source: bigchange.com

  • Vehicle tracking uses a separate tracker, not the tablet

    The vendor's vehicle tracking page says BigChange provides hard-wired vehicle tracking as standard, with a plug and go option that connects to the vehicle's OBD-II port and an optional CANbus and tacho connection for HGVs. Customers can be sent a tracking link showing their engineer's current location. The vendor does not say whether the JobWatch app uses the device's own GPS for this, so the GNSS receiver in a Tuga device should not be treated as a replacement for a BigChange tracker. Source: bigchange.com

  • Windows: no Windows app, office login in a web browser

    The vendor names Android and iOS for the mobile app and publishes no Windows app. The Login link on the vendor's home page goes to clients.bigchange.com, a web sign-in for the office system. No list of supported browsers or browser versions was found on the vendor's site. Source: clients.bigchange.com

Worth knowing. BigChange publishes no Windows app and no list of supported browsers, so the Tuga W10 is not recommended here: it would only reach the office system through a browser sign-in, and the engineer features (worksheets, photos, signatures, barcode scanning and offline working) are in the Android and iOS app. BigChange publishes no RAM, storage or screen size requirement, so the A6's 4GB of RAM cannot be checked against a vendor figure; trial one first. The vendor does not say whether barcode scanning uses the camera or a scan engine, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine should not be bought for BigChange on that basis. Vehicle tracking uses BigChange's own hard-wired or plug and go trackers, and NFC is not mentioned by the vendor, so the GNSS and NFC on the A8, A10 and A6 are device features, not BigChange features.
Setting up

Getting BigChange running

  1. Ask your BigChange administrator to set the engineer or driver up as a mobile user and confirm which worksheets and workflows they will use.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install JobWatch by BigChange (package bigchangeapps.com.jobwatch, developer BigChange Limited), then sign in with the user's details.
  3. Allow camera access for photos and barcode scanning, and allow notifications so new jobs arrive.
  4. Before the first shift without signal, open the app while connected and check that the day's jobs have come through. The vendor states the app works offline but does not publish how its offline cache fills, so test a job with the device in flight mode, including photos and a signature, then reconnect and check it reaches the office.
  5. If you use BigChange vehicle tracking, keep the hard-wired or plug and go tracker in the vehicle. The vendor does not say the app replaces it.
  6. Fit the vehicle mounting dock for the A8 or A10, add the 12V DC car charger, or the car phone mount and belt holster for the A6. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

BigChange on a Tuga device

The Google Play listing for JobWatch by BigChange gives a minimum API level of 28, which is Android 9. BigChange does not publish a RAM, storage or screen size requirement, so there is nothing further to check against. The vendor states that the field service app works offline and that engineers can collect signatures without connectivity. It does not publish how much is stored on the device or how sync works, so test a job in flight mode on a trial unit before relying on it. The A8, A10 and A6 all run the Google Play app.

Do not plan on it. All three Android devices have GNSS receivers, but treat that as a feature of the device, not of BigChange.

Both meet the published Android 9 requirement.
